item.title: IASTM for Forearm Extensors
clinicalUse: Adjunct in lateral elbow/forearm pain when short-term symptom reduction helps exercise
patientPosition: Sitting with forearm supported, wrist relaxed.
contact: Instrument edge over extensor muscle mass, avoiding bony lateral epicondyle pressure and superficial radial nerve path.
forceDirection: Light-to-moderate longitudinal/oblique strokes along muscle/tendon region.
dosage: 30–90 seconds, up to a few minutes total.
steps: 2. Apply small lubricant amount if needed.
safety: Avoid open skin, anticoagulation concerns, acute hematoma.
item.visualCue: Tool glides over extensor mass → brief dose → grip re-test.

subTechniques.name: Common wrist extensors — IASTM
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve pain, movement tolerance or tissue-related function when this target is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Sitting or supine with the upper limb supported.
subTechniques.contact: Appropriate instrument edge over intact skin at Common wrist extensors with conservative pressure.
subTechniques.direction: Use light-to-moderate scanning/treatment strokes; bruising is not the goal.
subTechniques.dosage: Often 30–120 seconds per small area followed by active movement/loading.
subTechniques.reassess: Re-test the region's original pain, range or functional task.
